title: Naturality and subset expansion of ordered join insertion-remainder summands
statement:
Let $r\geq1$, let $I=\{0,\ldots,r-1\}$, and let $X_i$ be sets with specified $v_i\in X_i$ for $i\in I$. For each integer $q$, let $J_q$ be the free abelian group with specified $\mathbf Z$-basis in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-free-module] consisting of symbols $[(i_0,x_0),\ldots,(i_q,x_q)]$ with $i_0<\cdots<i_q$ in $I$ and $x_a\in X_{i_a}$ when $0\leq q<r$. Let $J_{-1}=\mathbf Z[\varnothing]$ with its empty-symbol basis, and let $J_q=0$ in all other degrees. Define degree-one homomorphisms $c_i$ by zero on symbols containing $i$ and by inserting $(i,v_i)$ with sign $(-1)^k$ on symbols missing $i$, where $k$ counts colors less than $i$. Define degree-zero $R_i$ by zero on symbols missing $i$ and by $R_i\sigma=\sigma-T_i\sigma$ otherwise, where $T_i$ replaces the color-$i$ vertex by $(i,v_i)$. All formulas are extended by integer linearity, and all components involving zero source or target groups are zero. For $0\leq i\leq r$ put $P_i=R_0\circ\cdots\circ R_{i-1}$, with $P_0=1$ and rightmost maps applied first. For any family of maps $u_i:X_i\to Y_i$, give $Y_i$ the chosen point $w_i=u_i(v_i)$ and define $J_q(u)$ by applying $u_i$ to each vertex and fixing the empty symbol. Then, in every integer degree,
$$J_{q+1}(u)c_{i,q}^{v}=c_{i,q}^{w}J_q(u),\qquad J_q(u)R_{i,q}^{v}=R_{i,q}^{w}J_q(u).$$
No $u_i$ is required to be injective. For a basis symbol $\sigma$ let $C\subseteq I$ be its color set and $k_i=\#\{j\in C:j<i\}$. The individual summand $P_ic_i\sigma$ is zero if $i\in C$ or if some $j<i$ is absent from $C$. Otherwise, for $A\subseteq\{0,\ldots,i-1\}$ let $\sigma_{i,A}$ be obtained from $\sigma$ by inserting $(i,v_i)$ in increasing-color order and replacing the vertices of precisely the colors in $A$ by their chosen vertices. Then
$$P_ic_i\sigma=\sum_{A\subseteq\{0,\ldots,i-1\}}(-1)^{k_i+|A|}\sigma_{i,A}.$$
The right side is the specified unreduced list of $2^i$ terms indexed by subsets $A$; equal output symbols may occur and remain uncollected. The list of coefficients, insertion colors and replacement subsets depends only on $r$ and $C$, and uses no equality tests between original and chosen vertices. The formula includes the empty symbol and top-degree symbols.

proof.text: By [def-weil-pbc-free-module], every chain has a unique finite integer expansion in the specified symbols. A finite expression assigned to each basis symbol therefore extends to a homomorphism by taking the same integer linear combinations, and equality of homomorphisms can be checked on symbols. The formulas for $c_i$, $R_i$ and $J(u)$ have respectively at most one, two and one terms, so this applies to all of them, even when different input symbols have the same image under $J(u)$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent ordered-join calculation below the continuous-cocycle descent route; explicit proof from the operators defined in this item, not a claim made in the blueprint. Calculation 1.

proof.text: Fix a symbol $\sigma$ with color set $C$. Applying $u$ changes no color or position. If $i\in C$, both sides of the insertion identity vanish. Otherwise both sides insert $(i,u_i(v_i))=(i,w_i)$ at position $k_i$, retain all other vertices as $(j,u_j(x_j))$, and have coefficient $(-1)^{k_i}$. This proves $J(u)c_i^v=c_i^wJ(u)$ on symbols and hence on chains by step 1; it uses no injectivity.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent ordered-join calculation below the continuous-cocycle descent route; explicit proof from the operators defined in this item, not a claim made in the blueprint. Calculation 2.

proof.text: If $i\notin C$, both sides of the remainder identity are zero. If $i\in C$, applying $u$ to $T_i^v\sigma$ replaces the $i$-vertex by $u_i(v_i)=w_i$ and sends every other vertex to its $u$-image, which is exactly $T_i^wJ(u)\sigma$. Thus both sides equal $J(u)\sigma-T_i^wJ(u)\sigma$. Linearity gives $J(u)R_i^v=R_i^wJ(u)$, including when the two displayed terms coincide and cancel.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent ordered-join calculation below the continuous-cocycle descent route; explicit proof from the operators defined in this item, not a claim made in the blueprint. Calculation 3.

proof.text: If $i\in C$ then $c_i\sigma=0$, so $P_ic_i\sigma=0$. Suppose $i\notin C$ and some $j<i$ is absent from $C$. The inserted symbol has color set $C\cup\{i\}$, still missing $j$. In the composite $R_0\circ\cdots\circ R_{i-1}$, factors with index greater than $j$ act first. Each sends any symbol to zero or to a difference of symbols with the same color set. Consequently all terms still miss $j$ when $R_j$ is applied; that factor kills them, and every remaining factor sends zero to zero. This proves the other asserted vanishing without interchanging any factors.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent ordered-join calculation below the continuous-cocycle descent route; explicit proof from the operators defined in this item, not a claim made in the blueprint. Calculation 4.

proof.text: Assume every color less than n occurs in a face tau. Prove by induction on n that P_n[tau] is the sum over A subset {j : j<n} of (-1)^|A| [replace_A(tau)], in every degree (symbolTerm is zero for wrong cardinality). For n=0 the sole subset is empty and replacement is the identity. For n+1, the actual rightmost-first definition gives P_(n+1)=P_n composed with R_n. Since n occurs, this sends [tau] to P_n[tau]-P_n[replace_{n}(tau)]. Apply the induction hypothesis to both terms: replacement preserves colors. Composing replacements replaces their union. Partition subsets of {j : j<n+1} according as they contain n, using the powerset-insert sum formula; n is absent from every old subset, so adding it raises cardinality by one and negates the coefficient. This proves the induction. Apply it with n=i and tau=insert_i(sigma), then multiply by (-1)^k_i. The identity (-1)^(k_i+|A|)=(-1)^k_i*(-1)^|A| gives the exact signed list sum.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent ordered-join calculation below the continuous-cocycle descent route; explicit proof from the operators defined in this item, not a claim made in the blueprint. Calculation 5.

proof.text: The induction retains one formal term for each subset, even when chosen vertices already equal the original vertices. Its branching tests only membership of a color in a subset, never equality of vertices. The subset choices, insertion color and coefficient $(-1)^{k_i+|A|}$ depend only on $r,C,i$, and there are $2^i$ choices. For the empty symbol $C=\varnothing$, the $i=0$ summand is $[(0,v_0)]$ and every $i>0$ summand vanishes by step 4. For a top-degree symbol $C=I$, every insertion is zero. All identities involving other degrees hold as equalities of zero homomorphisms: if the source is zero this is automatic, and the only nonzero source with zero insertion target is the top degree just checked. Thus the conclusions include all stipulated degrees.

lean.statement: theorem functorialExpansion (r : ℕ) (hr : 1 ≤ r) (X : Fin r → Type u) (v : ∀ i : Fin r, X i) : (∀ (Y : Fin r → Type v) (f : ∀ i : Fin r, X i → Y i) (q : ℤ) (i : Fin r), (chainMap f (q + 1)).comp (insertion v i q (q + 1)) = (insertion (fun j ↦ f j (v j)) i q (q + 1)).comp (chainMap f q) ∧ (chainMap f q).comp (remainder v i q) = (remainder (fun j ↦ f j (v j)) i q).comp (chainMap f q)) ∧ (∀ (q : ℤ) (σ : Symbol X q) (i : Fin r), ((i ∈ σ.val.colors ∨ ∃ j : Fin r, j < i ∧ j ∉ σ.val.colors) → (remainderPrefix v i.val (q + 1)) (insertion v i q (q + 1) (Finsupp.single σ 1)) = 0) ∧ (i ∉ σ.val.colors → (∀ j : Fin r, j < i → j ∈ σ.val.colors) → (remainderPrefix v i.val (q + 1)) (insertion v i q (q + 1) (Finsupp.single σ 1)) = ((summandRecipe r σ.val.colors i).map (fun t ↦ t.1 • symbolTerm X (q + 1) (replaceColors v t.2.2 (insert v t.2.1 σ.val)))).sum)) ∧ (∀ (C : Finset (Fin r)) (i : Fin r), (summandRecipe r C i).length = 2 ^ i.val)
